text: P1 rwb-source-data keeps the interaction ledger and the EFS intake rule (interaction, efs_ledger_outcome); P3 keeps the case timeline API and P2 reads the ledger through P1's contract.
why: The R-PREC default ruling and DP-18 name P1, while TSD P3 v3 and TSD P2 v3 define the tables and the API tag says P3.
read: Plan Appendix R §R3 default ruling; plan DP-18; Architecture v5 slide 15; TSD P3 v3 T3.1; TSD P2 v3 T3.1
impact: P1, P3 and P2 DB and APP stories; no foreign keys across the ledger

text: P1 owns the daily case_list_row projection (built for JOB-04); P3 owns the case list API and screen under the default ruling.
why: TSD P1 v3 owns and builds the row table, the default ruling names the case list API for P3, and both are true of different artefacts.
read: TSD P1 v3 T3.1; FSD P1 v3 in scope; Plan Appendix R §R3 default ruling; Architecture v5 slide 44 JOB-04
impact: P1 and P3 DB stories; the case list read path

text: P7 rwb-decision owns rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case; each service evaluates a local copy and never reads the registry tables.
why: The default ruling, Architecture v5 and the Drools design place rule governance in P7; TSD P4 v3 and TSD P3 v3 declare the tables and the admin APIs in P4 and P3.
read: Plan Appendix R §R3 default ruling; Architecture v5 slides 14, 27 and 41; Temporal and Drools design slide 15; TSD P4 v3 T3.1; TSD P3 v3 T3.1
impact: P7, P4 and P3 contract and DB stories; DP-04 embedded Drools per service

text: P4 rwb-access owns delegation_limit (the DoA table); P3 keeps only non-DoA parameters and reference data.
why: Architecture v5 puts the DoA table in rwb_access and TSD P4 v3 defines it, while the Drools design calls the limits versioned reference data.
read: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41; TSD P4 v3 T3.1; Temporal and Drools design (delegation limits as reference data)
impact: P4 and P7 approval routing; P3 reference-data stories

text: P3 rwb-case owns lov_value as reference data; P4 owns only roles, scope, masking and DoA tables.
why: The default ruling gives reference data to P3; TSD P4 v3 lists lov_value in rwb_access.
read: Plan Appendix R §R3 default ruling; plan DP-07; TSD P4 v3 T3.1
impact: P3 and P4 DB stories; the list-of-values contract

text: S9 rwb-partner owns partner_user; P4 keeps the internal role model only.
why: Architecture v5 slide 41 gives partner users to S9; TSD P4 v3 defines partner_user in rwb_access.
read: Architecture v5 slide 41 S9; Architecture v5 slide 17 S9 DB line; TSD P4 v3 T3.1
impact: S9 partner portal and P4 access stories

text: The platform library (PLT) owns feature_flag and feature_flag_change; P2 serves the admin API against it.
why: The default ruling gives feature flags to the platform library; TSD P2 v3 defines the tables and the API tag says P2.
read: Plan Appendix R §R3 default ruling; TSD P2 v3 T3.1; API Specification v3 /feature-flags and /admin/feature-flags
impact: PLT library stories and the P2 admin contract

text: PLT owns the outbox, inbox and idempotency tables as library objects; every service creates its own copy in its rwb_* schema through the template.
why: Architecture v5 slide 20 gives every service an outbox and an inbox and DP-09 puts them in the PLT library; TSD P2 v3 lists them in rwb_integration.
read: Architecture v5 slides 11 and 20; plan DP-09 (RWB-PLT-TE006); TSD P2 v3 T3.1
impact: PLT service template; every service DB story; no shared inbox table across services

text: P2 rwb-integration owns job_catalog; each service keeps its own Temporal Schedules and does not write rows for them.
why: TSD P2 v3 defines the table and /admin/scheduled-jobs is x_module P2, while /admin/jobs is x_module P1 and Architecture v5 retires the shared Quartz job table.
read: TSD P2 v3 T3.1; API Specification v3 /admin/jobs and /admin/scheduled-jobs; Architecture v5 slide 44
impact: P2 operations console; the per-service Schedule catalogues

text: P5 rwb-document owns retention_rule; P1 drops its copy.
why: Architecture v5 places retention in rwb-document including JOB-17; TSD P1 v3 keeps retention_rule in rwb_source_data.
read: Architecture v5 slides 16, 41 and 44 JOB-17; TSD P1 v3 T3.1
impact: P5 and P1 DB stories; the monthly retention job

text: P5 rwb-document owns signature_request; P6 requests signatures through P5's contract.
why: Architecture v5 puts signatures in rwb_document; TSD P6 v3 defines the table in rwb_comms.
read: Architecture v5 slides 16 and 41 P5; TSD P6 v3 T3.1
impact: P5 and P6 contract and DB stories; the e-sign path from S2

text: P3 keeps the timer table as the screen projection; the clock is a durable Temporal timer in CaseWorkflow and no timer scan job runs.
why: Architecture v5 retires TimerDue and JOB-05, while the Physical Schema and TSD P3 still model a scanned timer table.
read: Architecture v5 slides 25, 42 and 44; Physical Schema v6 timer; TSD P3 v3 T3.1
impact: P3 DB and workflow stories; the GET /cases/{caseId}/timers projection

text: lake_copy_watermark is a P1 legacy table with no target; the data lake copy is gone and JOB-13 runs as continuous Kafka ingest in P7.
why: Architecture v5 removes the data lake and moves JOB-13 to rwb-decision, while the Physical Schema and TSD P1 v3 still keep the watermark.
read: Architecture v5 slides 37 and 44; plan DP-17; Physical Schema v6; TSD P1 v3 T3.1
impact: P1 DB story (drop), P7 decision-ledger ingest; no lake export story

text: P1 keeps the dated DP04 copies dp_treatment and dp_guarantee_claim; S2 and S3 keep the live records.
why: TSD P1 v3 keeps the DP04 copies as data products, while Architecture v5 makes S2 and S3 the owners of treatments and guarantee claims.
read: TSD P1 v3 T3.1; FSD P1 v3 in scope; Architecture v5 slides 18 and 41
impact: P1 data-product loads; S2 and S3 event publishing

text: P1 owns valuation_ext as one of the four extension tables; the writer of stale_flag and age_days stays open under FSD P1 OQ-P1-05, and S1 keeps the route decision in rwb_valuation.
why: FSD P1 owns the extension tables but its open question leaves the appraisal writer undecided, and Architecture v5 gives valuations to S1.
read: FSD P1 v3 change note, OQ-P1-05 and A2.6; TSD P1 v3 T3.1; Architecture v5 slide 41 S1
impact: P1 extension-table story; S1 valuation story; the stale-appraisal rule
